questions.q: It is 18:30. The plate under the sign shows the time 8.00-17.00. Who may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: The plate showing the time limits sign 3.28 to the period from 8.00 to 17.00. At 18:30 the ban no longer applies, so the blue car may park. The red car is on the other side, where there is no sign.

questions.q: It is 10:00. The plate under the sign shows the time 8.00-17.00. Who may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: At 10:00, sign 3.28 with the 8.00-17.00 plate is in force, and parking on the blue car's side is prohibited. The red car is on the other side, and the sign applies only on the side where it is placed.

questions.q: Today is 14 May. Who may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: Sign 3.29 prohibits parking only on odd days of the month. The 14th is an even day, so the blue car may park. There is no sign on the red car's side.

questions.q: Today is 15 May. Who may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: Sign 3.29 prohibits parking on odd days of the month, and the 15th is an odd day. The blue car is within the sign's zone. The red car is on the other side of the street, where there is no sign.

questions.q: Which of the drivers may stop here?
options: Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
Only the blue car
Only the red car
questions.explain: Sign 3.27 applies from where it is placed to the nearest intersection. The red car is within the sign's zone, while the blue car is already beyond the intersection, where the ban has ended. Both cars are more than 30 m from the intersection.

questions.q: Between the sign and the blue car there is only an exit from a yard. May the blue car stop here?
options: Yes: the sign applies only up to the exit from the yard
No: a yard exit does not interrupt the sign's effect
Yes, if it does not block the exit from the yard
questions.explain: An exit from a yard does not count as an intersection, so sign 3.27 does not stop applying there. The ban continues up to the nearest intersection.

options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: Sign 3.31 “End of all restrictions” also ends the parking ban of sign 3.28. The red car is between the signs, within the zone of the ban, and the blue car is already past sign 3.31.

questions.q: Which of the drivers may stop here?
options: Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
Only the blue car
Only the red car
questions.explain: A yellow solid line 1.4 along the edge of the carriageway prohibits stopping, and therefore parking too. The blue car is next to such a line. At the left-hand edge, where the red car is, there are no prohibitory markings.

questions.q: Which of the drivers may stop here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: A yellow broken line 1.10 prohibits only parking, so the blue car may stop. A yellow solid line 1.4 prohibits stopping, and it runs along the edge where the red car is.

questions.q: Which of the drivers may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: A yellow broken line 1.10 prohibits parking, and a yellow solid line 1.4 prohibits both stopping and parking. Neither the blue car nor the red car may be left parked here.

questions.q: The bus is running on an urban route. Who may stop here?
options: Only the blue passenger car
Only the bus
Both the bus and the blue car
Neither the bus nor the blue car
questions.explain: Sign 3.27 does not apply to route vehicles, and the bus may stand at the stop. The blue car is 25 m from the stop but within the zone of sign 3.27, so it may not stop there.

questions.q: A taxi with its taximeter on and a blue car have been standing here for 20 minutes. Who is allowed to park like this?
options: Both the taxi and the blue car
Neither the taxi nor the blue car
Only the blue car
Only the taxi
questions.explain: Sign 3.28 does not apply to taxis with the taximeter on. The blue car has been standing for more than 5 minutes with no boarding, alighting or unloading; this is parking, and it is prohibited here.

questions.q: You are a driver with a group I disability. There is a yellow broken line along the right-hand edge of the carriageway. May you leave your car here for an hour?
options: No: a yellow broken line prohibits parking for everyone
Yes: this line does not apply to such drivers
Yes, but you may stay no longer than 5 minutes
Yes, but only with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: A yellow broken line 1.10 prohibits parking, but it does not apply to vehicles driven by, or carrying, persons with group I or II disabilities (and also group III disabilities involving musculoskeletal disorders). The same exception is made for taxis with the taximeter on.

questions.q: Today is the 15th, and it is 14:00. Who may park here?
options: Only the blue car
Only the red car
Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
questions.explain: The 15th is an odd day, so sign 3.29 on the blue car's side prohibits parking. Sign 3.30 on the red car's side prohibits parking only on even days, so the red car may park today.

questions.q: You are approaching a sharp bend, and because of it you can see the road for only 60 m. May you stop on the carriageway right before the bend, as shown?
options: Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if you stay no longer than 5 minutes
No: visibility here is less than 100 m
questions.explain: You would be standing on the carriageway near a dangerous bend where visibility is less than 100 m. A driver coming round the bend may not be able to brake in time, so stopping here is prohibited.

questions.q: Which of the drivers may stop here?
options: Both the blue and the red car
Neither the blue nor the red car
Only the blue car
Only the red car
questions.explain: The blue car is blocking the exit from a yard. Stopping is prohibited where a vehicle would make it impossible for other vehicles to enter or leave. The red car is not in anyone's way.

questions.q: The blue car was here first. The red car has stopped opposite it, leaving about 2.5 m between the cars, and now a truck cannot get through. Who has broken the rules on stopping?
options: Only the blue car's driver
Only the red car's driver
Both drivers
Neither driver
questions.explain: Stopping is prohibited if there is less than 3 m left between your vehicle and a vehicle standing at the opposite edge, and this obstructs traffic. It was the red car's driver who created this obstruction by stopping opposite the blue car.

questions.q: There are two lanes in your direction, and oncoming traffic is separated by a solid line. May you stop at the right-hand edge, as shown?
options: No: stopping next to a solid line is prohibited in any case
Yes: a whole lane, over 3 m, remains before the solid line
Yes, but only for passengers to board or alight
questions.explain: Stopping is prohibited only if there is less than 3 m between the vehicle and a solid line and this obstructs traffic. Here there is a free lane to your left, and other vehicles can easily get past.
